Why PMP is (not) trapped in the C-family layouts

Course: main's wall_saddle_bumps_rand (static bumps + moving bodies; the wall slides in and stops on the axis at t = 6.4 s, which makes a symmetric saddle for an agent flying along the axis). Horizon N = 200, shared stopping rule, pair penalty Rc = 0.8 m. Every layout has one axis agent (0, 0) → (20, 0) plus side agents in ±y pairs. Each figure: rows K = 4 / 7, left Hopf–Lax-MPC (ours), right PMP-Shooting.

The one quantity that decides it: how close the nearest side agent is to the axis agent when the axis agent approaches the wall (x = 6.6 m, t ≈ 4.3 s). If a side agent is close, its pair interaction pushes the axis agent off the axis, the approach is no longer symmetric, the saddle disappears, and PMP slides past like everyone else. If the axis agent meets the wall alone (or with the side agents symmetric and far), the saddle survives and PMP converges onto it and stays.

* In the original layout at K = 7, PMP leaves one agent trapped at the wall, but it is a side agent that drifted onto the axis, and our method's cost is the same as PMP's (121.5 vs 117.7), so the demonstration is lost there. Note: my earlier wording "C_cross_before crosses at x ≈ 5" was wrong; the figures show the crossings at x ≈ 7–14. What makes it work is the 10 m head start of the axis agent.

1. Original C_axis_side: the trap disappears from K = 3

The red and orange side agents fly next to the axis agent (blue) up to the wall, about 1.3 m away. PMP's axis agent is pushed off the axis and passes; the agents marked "not arrived" stop short of their goals (the goal-hover effect, see section 5). Costs here come from runs with the old 0.3 m arrival radius, which run to the 30 s cap, so they are inflated for both methods.

2. C_lanes: side agents stay in their lanes (trap kept, no crossing)

KHopf–Lax-MPCPMP-Shooting
44/4 arrived, J = 12.02/4, axis agent trapped, J = 101.5 (8.5×)
77/7, J = 28.56/7, axis agent trapped, J = 100.5 (3.5×)

The cleanest trap and the biggest cost gap. Downside: the side agents never cross, so the only interaction is within each lane (column-following, like A_column) and some jostling at the lane goals.

3. C_cross_before: side agents start 10 m behind and cross later (trap kept, with crossing)

KHopf–Lax-MPCPMP-Shooting
44/4 arrived, J = 27.43/4, axis agent trapped, J = 52.4 (1.9×)
77/7, J = 78.66/7, axis agent trapped, J = 123.9 (1.6×)

The axis agent reaches the wall about 7 s before the side agents arrive, so it faces the saddle alone: PMP stops on it (ringed), ours escapes. The side agents then cross the course (x marks at x ≈ 7–14), weaving through the bumps and each other (minimum pair distance about 1.06 m), and PMP brings them home. This keeps the original C idea of crossing traffic. The cost gap is smaller because only one of the K agents is trapped.

4. C_cross_after: side agents start ahead (trap lost at K = 7)

Side agents start 2 m ahead and are 1.2 m from the axis agent at the wall approach: same failure as the original. At K = 4 PMP traps a side agent rather than the axis agent; at K = 7 nobody is trapped (PMP 7/7, J = 75.6 vs ours 72.0). Not usable.

5. Would a longer simulation (beyond 30 s) help?

No. In the original C_axis_side runs every agent that "did not arrive" was already parked by t ≈ 15–21 s: speed exactly 0 for the last 5 s, 0.33–0.72 m from its goal, unchanged until 30 s (a tracking equilibrium short of the goal, since the reference still asks for cruise speed at the path end). Examples: K = 4 agent 1 at 0.33 m from t = 20 s on; K = 7 agent 1 at 0.69 m; K = 9 agent 8 at 0.51 m from t = 25 s. With the new 0.8 m arrival radius all of them count as arrived (between 14.7 and 20.6 s), well inside 30 s, so more time is not needed.

Decision needed

  • C_cross_before: keeps crossing side traffic; one agent (the axis agent) is trapped by PMP at every tested K; cost gap 1.6–1.9×.
  • C_lanes: cleanest trap and largest gap (3.5–8.5×), but no crossing.
  • Or both. Next step for the chosen one(s): screen K = 3, 5, 6, 8, 9, 10 (Hopf–Lax-MPC + PMP, in parallel, about 1 h), then the sequential timing sweep.

Data: screening runs in multi_agent_interaction/results_demo_screen/; figures from plot_c_variants.py. All variants use the 0.8 m arrival radius except the original C_axis_side (0.3 m).
